dedupe_keys.name: okir mi van a kornyezetemben environmental data browser permitted sites emissions and contaminated areas in hungary

description: OKIR (Országos Környezetvédelmi Információs Rendszer) is Hungary's national environmental information system, a central database into which environmental, nature protection, waste and water authorities and the reporting operators enter their measurements and legally required returns; it is operated for the Ministry of Energy. Its public data browser 'Mi van a környezetemben?' (What is in my environment?) shows the disclosable environmental data of the clients of environmental administration and their objects: permitted sites and installations, contaminated areas and sampling points, with each client's environmental client code (KÜJ) and each site's area code (KTJ). Users can search by client name or by settlement and activity and see on a map which plants operate nearby and what they emit. OKIR also hosts Hungary's E-PRTR pollutant release and transfer register pages. Coverage is national; resolution is the individual site. Format and access: a web database browser and map (JavaScript application); no bulk download was seen. Licence: not stated. Free. Caveats: only data deemed disclosable are shown, the browser needs a JavaScript-capable browser, and water authority tasks moved to county government offices in October 2024. Simulation uses: locating industrial and waste sites and their emissions for hazard exposure and interdependency mapping near infrastructure. Related records: comparable to the Canada NPRI and the Australian National Pollutant Inventory.
